title: A correction fitted on 2001-2015 data reduced Ap forecast error on 2016-2025 dates
abstract: We tested updates to NOAA/USAF daily planetary Ap forecasts for the same target date. A linear correction fitted on 3,889 dates in 2001-2015 reduced test mean squared error by 9.27% on 3,247 dates in 2016-2025. A 27-day block interval was 4.58% to 13.43%. The correction kept about 70% of the day-3 to day-1 update. It gave a further 5.78% gain over a correction for mean bias alone. Results also gave lower average error with annual NOAA geomagnetic outcomes and a wider issue-time window. However, the correction raised error on 30 dates with reported Ap at least 50. Day-1 forecasts had lower squared error than day-3 forecasts, but the primary interval included no gain. This is a test of point forecasts under squared loss, not probability calibration or storm warning value. Missing reports, different outcome indices, one time split and conditional block intervals limit the result. The package gives code, source hashes, aggregate results, bootstrap statistics and audits. Raw data and record-level tables regenerate in external scratch.

display.caption: Annual forecast errors, test errors by update size, and test mean squared error. Bar labels give group sizes. The correction was fitted before the test period. Mean gains do not show a gain on severe storm days.
